key_insight: This paper proposes a brain-inspired generative model that can sample from cognitive maps to support goal-directed imagination and planning. The key advance is that it achieves planning and problem-solving using stochastic, compositional neural codes with only local synaptic plasticity.
problem_solved: AI systems often struggle to flexibly imagine future states, plan toward goals, and solve novel problems without heavy centralized training or handcrafted search procedures. This work addresses how to build a more biologically plausible mechanism for generating and evaluating possible action paths.
method: Uses cognitive maps as an internal structured representation of the environment and goals.
Employs neural sampling with stochastic computing to generate candidate future trajectories or solutions.
Encodes information compositionally, enabling reuse and combination of learned components.
Relies on local synaptic plasticity rather than global backpropagation-style updates.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a path toward more flexible and efficient planning systems that are closer to biological intelligence. It may inspire new architectures for model-based RL, generative planning, and neuromorphic or low-power AI.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing perception  cognitive map  sampling  imagined futures  goal selection

paper_title: Neural sampling from cognitive maps enables goal-directed imagination and planning
paper_authors: Hui Lin, Yukun Yang, Rong Zhao, Giovanni Pezzulo, Wolfgang Maass
